Compute the size of each topic

Source: R/corpus.R
topic_sizes.Rd

topic_sizes() returns the number and proportion of units in every topic of a fitted model and, with weights, the weighted size and share. The size of a topic can be counted in several ways: counted in distinct texts, it says how varied the content of the topic is; weighted by how often each text occurred, it says how much of the original corpus the topic accounts for.

A topic whose weighted share far exceeds its share of distinct texts is a small set of texts that are repeated many times. For a segmented model, a topic can be counted in segments or, with by = "document", in the documents that have at least one segment in it; a document with segments in several topics then counts in each of them, so the proportions need not sum to one. For a model fitted to documents, the two scales are the same.

Usage

topic_sizes(object, weights = NULL, by = c("segment", "document"))

Arguments

object

A topic model fitted by topics().

weights

Optional weights: the name of a numeric column carried in the model (for example "n" from dedupe()), or a numeric vector of non-negative weights, one per unit on the chosen scale. Default NULL.

by

Unit counted: "segment" (default), every modeled unit, or "document", the source documents.

Value

A base data frame with one row per topic and columns topic, label, n_documents, and proportion, followed by n_weighted and weighted_share when weights are given.

Conditions

An error of class sbert_bad_input when weights names a column that the model does not carry.

See also

dedupe() for the counts; topics(); as.data.frame() for the full tables; plot() with type = "sizes".

Examples

corpus <- head(dedupe(feedback_translations, column = "translation"), 600)
topic_model <- topics(corpus, n_topics = 6, column = "translation",
                      embeddings = feedback_embeddings)
topic_sizes(topic_model)
#>   topic                                                       label n_documents
#> 1     1   Where is the cow and the cake? Choose all the pictures...         223
#> 2     2            All the ones between the cat and the strawberry.         133
#> 3     3         What does “all the ones between the leaf and the...         131
#> 4     4 Are you sure you have fewer pictures in the red box than...          49
#> 5     5      In the top middle box, it means something is in the...          37
#> 6     6    It is not a person, does not have a hat, and is sitting.          27
#>   proportion
#> 1 0.37166667
#> 2 0.22166667
#> 3 0.21833333
#> 4 0.08166667
#> 5 0.06166667
#> 6 0.04500000
topic_sizes(topic_model, weights = "n")
#>   topic                                                       label n_documents
#> 1     1   Where is the cow and the cake? Choose all the pictures...         223
#> 2     2            All the ones between the cat and the strawberry.         133
#> 3     3         What does “all the ones between the leaf and the...         131
#> 4     4 Are you sure you have fewer pictures in the red box than...          49
#> 5     5      In the top middle box, it means something is in the...          37
#> 6     6    It is not a person, does not have a hat, and is sitting.          27
#>   proportion n_weighted weighted_share
#> 1 0.37166667        267     0.36081081
#> 2 0.22166667        162     0.21891892
#> 3 0.21833333        138     0.18648649
#> 4 0.08166667         76     0.10270270
#> 5 0.06166667         57     0.07702703
#> 6 0.04500000         40     0.05405405
